messages.subject: Logistic Regression
messages.body_plain:
Hi there:

In the most recent versions of Rattle, Logistic Regression has been
moved from Classification to Regression. Two comments about this:

1) It is been implemented using the command "lm" instead of "glm". So
what's been estimated is the linear probability model and not the
logistic regression. A few versions ago, the right command was used :
glm with family="binomial".

2) But more importantly, conceptually, logistic regression is a
classification method. I'm thinking about the way you evaluate its
performance. It's with confusion matrices, ROCR curves, etc. Just like
the other classification methods (trees, random trees). I think it
made a lot of sense to move linear regression and poisson regression
to the Regression section, but I think logit should have been left
there.

What do you think?

messages.subject: Re: Logistic Regression
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ernesto,

Thanks for the comments - I think you are spot on.  I'm actually
heading toward exactly what you are suggesting - cleaning up some old
code.

The regression side of things is under development (and at present in
the Beta version from Togaware - 2.3.22 - the pull down menu is
misleading - it actually is not doing logit). So yes it is now
using lm but I'm moving that to glm (from the Classification
paradigm) and will have the linear and poisson under Model for the
Regression paradigm.

Regarding the "Regression" radio button that used to appear under the
Model tab for the Classification paradigm, this is now "Neural
Network" and it generates exactly the same model (as I understand) but
uses the multinom function from the nnet package to deliver the
logistic regression.

Let me know what you think.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Just want to understand
messages.body_plain:
With Weka you will have to do a lot of data preparation outside of the
tool.  Although you can probably do some things with Knowledge Flow, I
always felt it was a bit limited and ended up just loading the
modelling dataset into Weka after it have been created elsewhere (ie
java/perl/python/sql/sas).  One benefit of Weka is there a an amazing
number of learners implemented.

With Rattle there are some data preperation operations you can do
within the interface, but you can always fall back to the R prompt and
code it up if need be.  Also if you build a model with Rattle you will
get the R code in the log which you can use to rebuild the model on a
regular basis (Weka can be invoked to build a model from the command
line but when you start chaining multiple operators & plugins together
it starts to get complicated).   There may also be some financial
packages for R which may be of interest to you.

Tony:  Impressive!  Do you still do this sort of data mining?  Thomas
A. Rathburn recently wrote a series of articles on data mining
financial markets which got me interested in this area.  One of his
observations was that it is easier to predict direction rather than
specific price points, which makes sense.  The articles are here:
http://www.b-eye-network.com/view/6386

Regards,
Shane

                 Pisa, Italy, December 15, 2008
                In conjunction with IEEE ICDM'08
          URL: http://datamining.it.uts.edu.au/dddm08/
********************************************************************

The Second International Workshop on Domain Driven Data Mining
(DDDM 2008) aims to provide a premier forum for sharing findings,
knowledge, insight, experience and lessons in tackling potential
challenges in discovering actionable knowledge from complex domain
problems, promote the interaction of and fill the gap between data
mining research and business expectations, and drive a paradigm
shift from traditional data-centered hidden pattern mining to
domain-driven actionable knowledge discovery.

Submission Instructions
-----------------------
Paper submissions should be limited to a maximum of 10 pages in the
IEEE 2-column format, the same as the camera-ready format (see the
IEEE Computer Society Press Proceedings Author Guidelines at
http://www.computer.org/portal/pages/cscps/cps/final/icdm06.xml).
All papers accepted for the workshop will be included in the
ICDM'08 Workshop Proceedings published by the IEEE Computer Society
Press. Selected papers from the workshop will be invited for
consideration of publication in a planned special issue of IEEE
Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (subject to approval
from TKDE).

messages.subject: Re: Export to SQL
messages.body_plain:
I have some very basic experimental code - but not yet useful. There
are problems in exporting some models to SQL. In particular, ensembles
generate very large SQL.

The PMML, in theory, can be loaded into Teradata Warehouse Miner which
will convert it to SQL. I've successfully tested this with single
decision trees.

I'm looking at exporting to PMML and C++ code in the near future. I
would imagine that pretty much the same parsing can be used to
generate SQL. Happy for anyone to contribute code to do so :-)

I have the C++ export working for randomForests (and we've done some
basic testing to show that a 500 tree forest exported as C++ can score
12 million rows of transactions in about 60 seconds on a Netezza data
warehouse.)

The proper solution would be to write a package to read PMML and
convert that to C++ or SQL. The short term solution will be to model
the C++ and SQL code generation on the PMML generating code in the
pmml package. Shouldn't be too hard......

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Recent updates to Rattle - Version 2.3.31
messages.body_plain:
Time for another update on progress with Rattle.

There has been some quite significant changes recently - hopefully
they are all improvements.

Overall details are available from

  http://rattle.togaware.com/changes.html

A new stable version will be released through CRAN soon, once the beta
release from rattle.togaware.com <http://rattle.togaware.com> has gone through testing. You can
install the beta version with:

  > install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com")

The most significant update has been the removal of the paradigm radio
buttons and the per
manent display of the Cluster and Associate tabs, as well as the
merging of the Data and Select tabs into one Data tab. I believe this
makes the interface simpler and more streamlined, and is in response
to a number of user requests.

If you try this new version, please let me know of any bugs. I expect
the version umber will increase a little over the next couple of days.

Regards,
Graham
